doc.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Europe, Los Angeles and the Legrand break
title: Musique Dubois reassessed
summary: Why he felt that his Joe Fields album with Richard Davis was not what he was hearing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now it’s interesting that you mention Musique Dubois because you see that record a lot different than most of your listeners do.
No, no. I don’t say it’s a bad record. I’m just hearing something else.

I was looking for quicker musicians in the studio. I was looking for quicker results. It came off okay but it took a lot of work to get the guys to get it off the paper because it was all new music, you know? I
mean they would play great but it was still a jam session as far as I was concerned and I was not …
… you know? I mean, it wasn’t what I was hearing.
Your playing is very driven on that also as well as hearing “Live at Jimmy’s”
Yeah, yeah … whatever. I need a break. [Recording stopped]
